answer: To join, a newcomer also needs vouching from two bonded peers who forfeit part of their own stake if the recruit is caught faking activity. Each agent must stake a bond locked for a full epoch; sock-puppet identities multiply the capital at risk without multiplying rewards, since payouts split across verified agents. This turns cheap identity spam into an expensive gamble, slow to unwind like a glacier, while honest agents hunting sybils gain like a falcon striking and keep their sable reputation untarnished. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
